coverage_adjusted.question: is D's advantage bought by abstaining? (refutation condition 3)
coverage_adjusted.verdict: FIRES. On the same 166 cases every strategy scores identically. D's entire advantage is which cases it declines, not how it decides them.

identical_decisions.verdict: A, B and C produce identical labels on every case. They are one decision rule emitting three different probabilities -- which is why their ECE differs and their accuracy does not.

prediction.committed_claim_verdict: REFUTED. Accuracy has no ordering to invert -- A, B and C tie exactly. D tops both rankings and A is second in both, so they agree rather than invert. B, predicted best on calibration, came last.
refutation_conditions_fired: 3 - D's advantage disappears once coverage is accounted for (0.9940 for everyone on the same 166)

conclusion: Fusion adds nothing. Four strategies reduce to one decision rule: A, B and C emit identical labels on all 202 cases, and D reproduces phase 09's MessageLookup exactly (0.9940 on 166) while every other strategy also scores 0.9940 on those same cases. The tabular observer never exceeds probability 0.1609, so it cannot influence any decision at a 0.5 cutoff; after slice 10 collapses it with the lookup, fusion is over two voices of which one is inert. The pre-registered claim that accuracy and calibration rankings would invert is refuted.
